intent: A size people misjudge: the camera visits each island as it is named, the to-scale bars make the winner 3 times the runner-up, a flash marks the ice sheet fact, and the population counter stops at a number smaller than a town.

v04.text: Greenland. Over 2 million square kilometres of island.

v05.text: Borneo is huge, and Madagascar is bigger than France. Greenland is almost 3 times bigger than either.

v06.text: About 80 percent of it is buried under a single ice sheet, which in places is up to 3 kilometres thick.

v07.text: Only around 56,000 people live on the whole island, most of them along the south west coast, around the small capital, Nuuk.

research.topic: Greenland is the largest island in the world at about 2,166,086 km² (Britannica; Statistics Greenland); New Guinea is second at about 786,000 km², Borneo third at about 748,000 km² and Madagascar fourth at about 587,000 km² (Britannica). Australia (7.7 million km²) is classed as a continent, not an island. About 80% of Greenland is covered by the Greenland Ice Sheet, up to about 3 km thick (NSIDC; Britannica). The population is about 56,000–57,000 (Statistics Greenland 2025), most living on the ice-free south-west coast; Nuuk, the capital, has about 20,000. Greenland is an autonomous territory of the Kingdom of Denmark.

myths.reality: Australia is counted as a continent; among islands Greenland is largest at about 2.17 million km², almost three times Borneo or New Guinea.

landscape.our_gap: Largest-island clips argue about Australia; nobody visits the candidates on the map, bars them to scale and lands the population counter on a number smaller than a town, as a quiz.
